analysis_scope: Source candidates, not runtime execution: the explicit root is an import root, not itself a package. Regular package __init__.py files are listed outermost first; namespace directories contribute no initializer. A source module blocks a dotted traversal beyond itself. From-import child candidates are conditional because an attribute may already exist. Conditions, aliases, sys.modules, search paths, loaders, extension modules and runtime package attributes are not evaluated. Initializer imports are inspected as separate sites, not recursively executed. Dynamic imports and wildcard expansion are omitted. No project code is imported; the existing explicit import graph is unchanged.
collection_scope: Complete means collection finished within the stated budgets, not that runtime imports are known. Hidden and conventional dependency directories, symlinks and nonregular files are skipped. Explicit AST imports only; parse issues and dynamic calls remain visible. Use a stable source tree. These are input-size limits, not CPU, memory or elapsed-time guarantees.
scope: Static source candidates only, not observed imports or execution order. Keys are source coordinates, not semantic identities across edits. Line shifts appear as removals/additions. Missing source can mean an external import; it does not establish a missing installation. Equality of CSV rows does not certify complete or safe source. Keep snapshot stderr evidence and inspect its issues and manifest.
